claim.quote: Measurement of the very rare $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ decay

date.note: date is the arXiv preprint submission date; publication is JHEP06(2021)093.

key_value.note: Branching ratio in units of 10^-11; stored as a bare count-like number because the ontology has no branching-ratio dimension. See key_value_text for the fully formatted value.

key_value_text.quote: BR$(K^+ \rightarrow \pi^+ \nu\bar{\nu}) = (10.6^{+4.0}_{-3.4} |_{\rm stat} \pm 0.9_{\rm syst}) \times 10 ^{-11}$ at 68% CL, based on the observation of 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events
key_value_text.value: BR(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (10.6+4.0-3.4|stat +- 0.9syst) x 10^-11, based on 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events

name: Measurement of the very rare K⁺ → π⁺νν̄ decay

significance.quote: This provides evidence for the very rare $K^+ \rightarrow \pi^+ \nu\bar{\nu}$ decay, observed with a significance of 3.4$\sigma$.

summary.plain: NA62 measured how often a positive kaon decays into a pion and two invisible neutrinos, a very rare decay, using its 2016 to 2018 data: 20 signal candidates over an expected background of 7.0 events. The paper says this provides evidence for the decay, observed with a significance of 3.4σ.
summary.technical: Branching-ratio measurement of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar from the 2016-2018 NA62 data set: BR = (10.6+4.0-3.4|stat ± 0.9syst)×10⁻¹¹ at 68% CL, based on 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events; the paper says this provides evidence for the decay, observed with a significance of 3.4σ.

title: Measurement of the very rare K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay
why_it_matters: The abstract says the measurement provides evidence for the very rare K⁺→π⁺νν̄ decay and gives a single event sensitivity of (0.839 ± 0.054)×10⁻¹¹, corresponding to 10.0 events assuming the Standard Model branching ratio of (8.4 ± 1.0)×10⁻¹¹.
